S1_known_answer_control_P1b.purpose: Inherited CTRL-RT-4 / CTRL-RT-6: a known-answer control on the estimator callable itself, BEFORE its output is differenced against anything. Four batches of GOAL-MLKEM-003 argued about this callable and none covered it.

checks.note: This is the name collision the predecessor campaign argued about: the module-level `dual_hybrid` in lwe_dual.py wraps DH = DualHybrid(), a different attack from the MATZOV instance the public name resolves to.
MATZOV.Hf(Xs) = (1/2 + ln(sqrt(2 pi) sigma) + ln(coth(pi^2 sigma^2)))/ln 2

checks.description: MATZOV.Nf == independent reimplementation over a 6-point grid
checks.note: independent reimplementation includes an independent deltaf for beta>40, deltaf(beta) = (beta/(2 pi e) (pi beta)^(1/beta))^(1/(2(beta-1)))

checks.description: Nf is independent of p when k_fft == 0
checks.note: Known answer by inspection of the formula: with k_fft=0 both p-bearing terms (k_fft*log p, exp(k_fft/3 (sigma_s pi/p)^2)) vanish. Confirms OBJ-1: with no FFT sub-block split, p has NO referent in this design.

checks.description: Hf returns BITS while log(p), log(1/mu) are NATURAL logs
checks.note: RECORDED OBSERVATION, not a claim that the estimator is wrong: the sum k_enum*Hf(Xs) + k_fft*log(p) + log(1/mu) adds a term in bits to two terms in nats. MATZOV.cost's T_guess uses 2**(k_enum*H), which confirms H is intended in bits. Consequence for this task: any reading of the log-term that uses k_enum carries an additional factor-ln2 ambiguity beyond the referent ambiguity of OBJ-1.

checks.description: Nf independent of beta_bkz when beta_sieve == m + k_lat
checks.note: Known answer by inspection: the factor deltaf(beta_bkz)^(m+k_lat-beta_sieve) has exponent 0. This is why the length sub-comparison in S2 is free of the beta ambiguity: the measured run sieved the FULL d=60 lattice.

checks.description: LWE.dual_hybrid(Kyber512, RC.ADPS16) against the estimator's own documented value in estimator/lwe.py docstring line 55: rop ~ 2^115.5, beta 395, p 5, zeta 0, t 40, beta' 395
checks.note: Strongest form of the control: the exact public callable reproduces a value documented in the pinned repository itself, at cryptographic parameters.

S2_wellposedness_P1.question: Does an (m, k_enum, k_fft, p, beta_bkz, beta_sieve) tuple exist that makes MATZOV.Nf well-posed on the measured design?

design_facts.sieve: LLL then g6k bgj1_sieve over the FULL d=60 dual lattice
design_facts.note: The design scores candidate secrets that differ from s on any of all n coordinates, and it obtains its vectors from a sieve run on the full (m+n)-dimensional dual lattice, in which the y-part of every vector is short.

S2_wellposedness_P1.impossibility_argument: MATZOV.Nf line 540 fixes k_lat = n - k_fft - k_enum, so k_lat + k_fft + k_enum = n identically. Requirement R1 (the sieved lattice has dimension m + k_lat, and the measured one has dimension m + n) forces k_lat = n, hence k_enum + k_fft = 0. Requirement R2 (candidates are enumerated over all n secret coordinates) forces k_enum + k_fft = n = 25. Both hold only if n = 0. The admissible set is EMPTY, verified by exhaustive enumeration over all 351 integer pairs (k_enum, k_fft) with k_enum + k_fft <= n.

pinned_by_the_run.beta_bkz: IRRELEVANT (not a free choice, and not a fit): the only place beta_bkz enters Nf is deltaf(beta_bkz)^(m + k_lat - beta_sieve), whose exponent is 0 when beta_sieve = m + k_lat = d = 60. Verified as known-answer control KA-5.
pinned_by_the_run.note: These three ARE determined by the measured run. The obstruction is confined to (k_enum, k_fft, p), and through k_lat it then contaminates the length model too -- see 'sub_comparison_C'.

S2_wellposedness_P1.p_has_no_referent: The design performs no FFT sub-block split, so k_fft = 0 under any reading that respects the vector family, and then Nf is identically independent of p (known-answer control KA-3). The factor exp(k_fft/3 (sigma_s pi/p)^2) -- which exists precisely to charge the adjacent-FFT-bin penalty, i.e. the very near-miss phenomenon batch 1 observed -- is therefore identically 1 and untestable here.

sub_comparison_C.name: the LENGTH model, under the reading that matches the vector family
sub_comparison_C.why_well_posed: Under reading R-A (k_lat = n, k_enum = k_fft = 0) the vector family Nf describes IS the measured one: a sieve over the m+k_lat = d = 60 dimensional dual lattice. beta_sieve = 60 is a fact of the run, not a fit, and beta_bkz drops out (KA-5). So lsigma_s is fully determined with no free parameter.
sub_comparison_C.what_is_still_not_well_posed: R-A's log-term is log(1/mu) alone: under R-A no candidate is enumerated, so the measurement's candidate axis has no counterpart. This sub-comparison therefore tests the LENGTH/advantage half of the law only, which is exactly INGREDIENT 1.

S2_wellposedness_P1.answer: NO SUCH TUPLE EXISTS. The admissible set is empty by exhaustive enumeration. (m, beta_sieve, beta_bkz) are pinned by the run; (k_enum, k_fft, p) admit no consistent assignment. The comparison is therefore made against the law's two SEPARABLE INGREDIENTS.

S5_per_candidate_group_P3.never_pooled: Statistics are reported per candidate group only. No pooled wrong-candidate statistic is computed anywhere in this file (INT-3, DEC-20260803-d810d0).

S5b_success_vs_subsample_size.note: Success = correct secret's mean score exceeds every member of the named group, on a random subsample of size N'. Subsampling holds the LENGTH distribution fixed, whereas a genuinely smaller sieve returns SHORTER vectors and would do better (RT OBJ-5).

S6_ingredient1_per_vector_advantage.law: per-vector advantage  E_e[cos(2 pi x.e/q)] = exp(-2 pi^2 sigma_e^2 ||x||^2 / q^2)
S6_ingredient1_per_vector_advantage.law_source: MATZOV.Nf's exponential factor exp(4 (l sigma pi/q)^2) is 1/advantage^2 with advantage = exp(-2 (l sigma pi/q)^2); this is the per-vector half of the law, and it is separable from the log-term that has no referent here (S2).

sub_comparison_C_length_model.note: Well-posed piece identified in S2. MODELED quantities are labelled; MEASURED quantities are labelled.

S7_ingredient2_iid_candidate_noise.law: wrong-candidate mean scores are the average of N independent contributions, so sd = sqrt(Var(score)/N); for a candidate whose phase is uniform mod q this is sqrt(1/(2N)).
S7_ingredient2_iid_candidate_noise.note_on_offsets: The secret_distribution and near_miss groups are NOT centred at 0: their phases retain y.(s-c) with s-c small, so exp(-a_y)-type retention applies. a_y (measured) = 0.1586, exp(-a_y) = 0.8534.

S8_nulls_P2.corrective_rule: DEC-20260803-d810d0 PD-1: every null names the OBJECT whose removal it tests.

nulls.name: vector-null: random directions of matched ||x||
nulls.removes_object: THE SIEVE DATABASE ITSELF -- its lattice membership, its integrality, the exact 3-term algebraic relations among its vectors, and its ball saturation structure. This is the object whose independence MATZOV.Nf asserts.
nulls.preserves: N, m, q, sigma_e, and the exact empirical ||x|| distribution (each surrogate vector has the norm of the sieve vector it replaces), hence a_x is identical by construction.
nulls.can_it_fail: YES. If the sieve database's concentration behaviour were a property of sieving, the surrogate would not reproduce it.
nulls.statistic: mean_i cos(2 pi x_i.e / q) for the correct secret, over 1000 fresh error draws

modeled_analytic_sd_this_task.derivation: MODELED, derived in this task and not taken from MATZOV: for vectors spread over directions, the database mean depends on e essentially through ||e||^2 only, S(e) ~ exp(-a_x ||e||^2/(m sigma^2)); with Var(||e||^2) = 2 m sigma^4 this gives sd(S) ~ S * a_x * sqrt(2/m), independent of N.

nulls.name: independent-error null: the law taken literally
nulls.removes_object: THE SHARED m-DIMENSIONAL ERROR VECTOR e -- the single object that couples the N per-vector contributions. Each vector is scored against its own fresh error draw, which is what 'N independent samples' literally means.
nulls.preserves: the sieve database exactly, N, m, q, sigma_e.
nulls.can_it_fail: YES. If the coupling were negligible, this would match the sieve database's variance.
nulls.statistic: mean_i cos(2 pi x_i.e_i / q), independent e_i per vector, over 1000 draws

nulls.name: target-null: b replaced by uniform on Z_q^m (BATCH-d2a728's null)
nulls.removes_object: THE LWE STRUCTURE IN THE TARGET b. It does NOT remove or perturb the sieve database.
nulls.preserves: the sieve database exactly, the candidates, and the scoring code.
nulls.can_it_fail: NO -- and this is why it is reproduced here only for continuity and reported with that label attached. With b uniform on Z_q^m, x.b is uniform mod q for every fixed nonzero x, so every phase is uniform and every mean score is 0 in expectation. Any code that reads b passes it. (RT-20260803-4064e1 OBJ-2; DEC-20260803-d810d0 PD-1.)
nulls.statistic: per-candidate mean score over 1000 fresh uniform targets
nulls.pooled_statistic_deliberately_not_report: Batch 1's '18 of 33' pooled three populations its own producer calls non-exchangeable. Per group is reported above; no pooled rank is computed here.

nulls.name: m-sweep and N-sweep of the vector-null surrogate (CTRL-RT-2)
nulls.removes_object: THE SIEVE DATABASE (as NULL-V) while additionally VARYING m and N, the two parameters that would have to control the effect if it were, respectively, a small-dimension artifact or a genuine loss of independent samples.
nulls.preserves: a_x, by reusing the measured ||x|| distribution at every m.
nulls.can_it_fail: YES. If the variance inflation were a loss of independent samples from the database, N_eff would depend on N.
